changes: Normalized paksa to 'śukla', tithi to 'dvitīyā (followed by tṛtīyā)', weekday to 'Monday (somavāra)'.
Separated nakshatra and yoga, and identified 'valiyāna' as the yoga Varīyān.
Expanded the notes on the Newari scribal formula and the fragmentary 'iti sa(‥)yā'.
Scribe identification, NS era and ce_approx 1800 confirmed.

date.as_written: samvat 920 māghamāse śuklapakṣe || dvitīyāparatṛtīyāyāṃn tithau || śatabhiṣānakṣatre || valiyānayoge (!) || somavāsare

notes: The Newari formula 'thva kuhnu … daivajñakīrttinārāyanana coya dhunakā juro' means 'on this day … the writing was completed by the astrologer (daivajña) Kīrtinārāyaṇa'. In 'nārāyanana', the final '-na' is the Newari ergative ending. 'iti sa(‥)yā' before the name is fragmentary and may be the end of a phrase or an epithet; it is not read as a separate person. The 'yādṛśaṃ…' and 'bhagnapṛṣṭha…' verses are standard scribal verses. NS 920 Māgha corresponds to about January–February 1800 CE. The catalogue fields agree with this reading.
